_comment: Permissions are a thin CONVENIENCE layer, not a security layer. The real enforcement boundary is the firewall + bash-guard universal blocks + the Docker sandbox + the auto-mode classifier. The allow set covers universal-safe, stack-agnostic commands and a broad workspace write allowance so cross-repo (control-plane + code) development is frictionless; per-stack tooling (npm/cargo/gcloud/…) is intentionally NOT listed here and is handled by auto mode. The deny set is a thin backstop only.
